metadata.title: Taxonomic tree of order Scorpiones C. L. Koch, 1837
metadata.description: This work was largely completed on 8th December 2024, with most synonyms added after 14th August 2025, and submitted on 1st August 2026 as the first version. I would like to thank Professor Victor Fet for his guidance with regard to the synonyms. For future update log, see Zenodo. This taxonomic tree will not be updated absent supraspecific changes (e.g., intergeneric transfer, generic or familial revision). For semi-annual taxonomic update, see Factanonverba. For timely species-level update (e.g., new species, synonyms, revalidations), see The Scorpion Files Newsblog. It must be clarified that all nominal taxa included here merely reflect the latest "consensus", not that they are all "true" valid species. Certain genera and species are clearly invalid and warrant formal synonymization. Some debatable species are marked by * (e.g., species undergone synonymization and revalidation within a short interval, which are either retained as valid species or as synonyms with a question mark). For species described by Amir et al. and Caribbean Heteronebo species, see my earlier informal publications. I finally decided to add Chinese names for all extant taxa because I don't want this work to be conveniently exploited by some kleptoparasitic Chinese amateurs who comfortably and conveniently thrive on my work while disparaging my translations of scientific names.

metadata.title: Limbic Encephalitis Presenting with Faciobrachial Dystonic Seizures After History of Successfully Treated Thymoma Type B-3 with Excellent Neurocognitive Outcome with Early Immunotherapy
metadata.description: Paraneoplastic Encephalitis syndromes are an inflammatory condition of the brain and central nervous system often associated with cancer diagnoses. In many cases, the paraneoplastic encephalitis is often the initial presentation for an underlying cancer. Limbic encephalitis, a form of paraneoplastic encephalitis, involves inflammatory changes specific to the limbic structures such as the hippocampi, hypothalamus, and limbic cortex. Numerous paraneoplastic and limbic encephalitides have been studied and associated with specific anti-body associated autoimmune processes. Anti-LGI1 encephalitis, is a form of limbic encephalitis associated with antibodies to the LGI1 protein and can present with stereotypical faciobrachial dystonic seizures (FBDS). We describe a case of FBDS in a patient with prior history of treated Thymoma Type B-3, who presented with faciobrachial dystonic seizures. Patient was found to have Anti-LGI1 antibodies on paraneoplastic work up and treated with intravenous immunoglobulin with remarkable response and continued improvement with seizure control and neurocognitive outcome with immunotherapy.

metadata.title: Simultaneous identities of the golden ratio and Euler's identity, formally verified in Lean 4 over the known Mersenne prime exponents
metadata.description: We present a sustained study of a single object followed across representations, where the content lives in the equivalences between them. We prove and formally verify in Lean 4 that the golden ratio φ=(1+√5)/2 satisfies simultaneously twelve identities across five canonical structures. The central clause is 3φ^{σ(p)}=2^p, specialisable to the 52 known Mersenne prime exponents. The verification is conducted against Mathlib4 with 0 sorry.

metadata.title: Perfect broadband sound absorber metamaterial for noise reduction in a rocket launch
metadata.description: Metamaterials based on Helmholtz resonators represent alternatives for noise mitigation applications where traditional materials can not be used due to the environmental conditions. One such case is found in the extreme acoustic event caused by a rocket launch. Metamaterials can also be designed on demand to act on the sound waves at a specific frequency range, which depends on the particular application. In this work we present the design procedure of a metamaterial panel, with a potential use for noise mitigation during a rocket launch. The proposed sound absorber presents almost perfect sound absorption in a prescribed bandwidth. The geometrical parameters of a unit cell, the building block of the panel, are obtained by using the transfer matrix method, and the use of optimization algorithms. The effective acoustical parameters of the designed metamaterial are also obtained. Using the effective parameters, the acoustical response of a panel built from an array including a large number of unit cells is numerically computed. Finally, experiments in an impedance tube that validate the theoretical results are presented.

metadata.title: Acoustic field prediction during the launch of rockets
metadata.description: This work presents the prediction of noise generated during the launch of space rockets. A semiempirical model was applied, using as input data the physical and geometric characteristics of the jet of gases propelled by the rocket, which acts as the primary source of noise. The model is based on the one originally proposed by Eldred back in 1971 and its subsequent modifications. We expanded the model with expressions for the estimation of the acoustic power of noise sources. To validate the prediction in a particular case, we have considered the launch of the VEGA rocket from European Space Agency, at the launchpad located in Kourou (French Guiana). Using as reference experimental data recorded during a launch, the study confirms that the semi-empirical model predicts the acoustic field generated during the launch with great precision, especially in the low and medium frequencies, which are the most interesting from the point of view of impact that this noise has on the rocket and its load.

metadata.title: Productividad del cultivo de fresa 'monterrey' (fragaria x ananassa duch.) en hidroponía vertical: Influencia solución nutritiva-sustrato
metadata.description: Este estudio, realizado en Antonio Ante, Ecuador, evaluó el impacto de tres soluciones nutritivas y tres sustratos en el rendimiento de fresa 'Monterrey' cultivada en un sistema hidropónico vertical. En 48 m², el experimento se estructuró mediante un arreglo de parcelas divididas con nueve tratamientos con cuatro réplicas. Las variables evaluadas fueron biomasa aérea, rendimiento, eficiencia en el uso de agua, sólidos solubles totales y análisis beneficio-costo. La solución nutritiva con concentraciones de 100 (N), 90 (P), 250 (K), 60 (Ca), 30 (Mg) y 20 (S) kg ha⁻¹ (Solución 2) combinada con el sustrato 10% cascarilla de arroz, 80% fibra de coco y 10% pomina (Sustrato 2) fue la más efectiva. Este tratamiento alcanzó un rendimiento de 21,60 t ha⁻¹, la mayor eficiencia del uso del agua (0,83 kg m⁻³) y un contenido de sólidos solubles totales de 10,82 °Brix. Asimismo, mostró la mejor relación beneficio-costo, generando USD 3,75 por cada dólar invertido. Los resultados demuestran que la combinación Solución 2 con el Sustrato 2 optimiza la productividad, calidad de fruto y rentabilidad en la producción hidropónica vertical de fresa. Esta propuesta representa una alternativa viable para que los pequeños agricultores de la región mejoren sus rendimientos y rentabilidad comparado con los cultivos tradicionales en suelo.

metadata.title: Bleach: A Programming Language for Teaching Compilers
metadata.description:
DESCRIPTION

Bleach is a dynamically typed, object-oriented programming language designed for undergraduate Compilers / Programming Language Implementation courses. This deposit is the reference implementation: a single-translation-unit C++17 tree-walk interpreter with zero third-party dependencies, its 44-case regression test suite, and 11 algorithm/data-structure programs used to validate the language.

It is the artifact accompanying the paper “Bleach: A Programming Language for Teaching Compilers”, accepted for publication into SBLP 2026 (30th Brazilian Symposium on Programming Languages), part of CBSoft 2026.

For convenience, the entire repository is uploaded as a single compressed archive, Bleach-main.zip. After extracting the archive, the repository follows the structure described below.

What is Bleach?

Teaching-oriented languages for undergraduate Compilers courses occupy a narrow design space: COOL and MiniJava stay deliberately minimal and statically typed, and ChocoPy targets compilation rather than interpretation. Bleach fills the gap with a language built for interpretation, so that scanning, parsing, resolving, and evaluation can each be inspected and modified as a self-contained assignment.

The interpreter is structurally inspired by Lox, from Crafting Interpreters, and extends it with multi-line comments, do-while and for loops, elif clauses, a ternary operator, a list type, break/continue statements, an expanded standard library, and a resolver that statically detects ten distinct classes of scoping and control-flow errors before execution begins.

Example — Fibonacci with elif

function fibonacci(n) {
  if(n <= 0){ return 0; }
  elif(n == 1){ return 1; }
  else{ return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2); }
}

let n = 10;
std::io::print("The", n, "th Fibonacci number is:", fibonacci(n));
// The 10th Fibonacci number is: 55

WHAT THIS DEPOSIT CONTAINS

The contents of the repository are uploaded as a single Bleach-main.zip file for convenience. Once extracted, the folder structure is as follows. 

Bleach/
├─ src/                              # C++17 interpreter, single translation unit (main.cpp)
│  ├─ lexer/                         # Scanner
│  ├─ parser/                        # Recursive-descent parser
│  ├─ resolver/                      # Static resolver — scoping & control-flow checks
│  ├─ interpreter/                   # Tree-walk evaluator and runtime
│  ├─ error/                         # Error types
│  ├─ utils/                         # Shared runtime data structures
│  └─ Makefile
├─ scripts/                          # build / run / clean / test entry points
├─ tests/
│  ├─ valid_bleach_programs/         # 44 .bch inputs — expressions, native_functions, statements
│  ├─ valid_bleach_programs_output/  # expected stdout per test
│  └─ algorithms_and_data_structures/ # 11 sorting / search / graph programs
├─ Dockerfile                        # pins gcc:13-bookworm for a reproducible build
├─ LICENSE                           # MIT
└─ README.md

REQUIREMENTS

  • Hardware: none special — a single-threaded tree-walk interpreter; any machine able to run a C++ compiler with well under 1 GB RAM and 100 MB disk is sufficient.
  • Operating system: Linux and macOS natively; on Windows use Docker or WSL2 (the build/run scripts are Bash and rely on a POSIX shell).
  • Native build: a C++17-capable g++ (GCC 9+), GNU make, and bash. No external libraries — the interpreter depends only on the C++ standard library.
  • Docker route (recommended): Docker Engine 20.10+. This pins the exact compiler (gcc:13-bookworm) used to validate this artifact.

GETTING STARTED

Option A — Docker (recommended)

Pins the exact compiler used to validate this artifact (gcc:13-bookworm); no local toolchain required.

$ git clone https://github.com/vmmc2/Bleach.git && cd Bleach
$ docker build -t bleach-interpreter .
$ docker run -it bleach-interpreter
# inside the container, already positioned in scripts/
$ ./bleach_run.sh                 # interactive REPL
$ ./bleach_run.sh program.bch      # run a .bch file

Option B — Build from source

Requires a C++17-capable g++ (GCC 9+), GNU make, and bash. Linux and macOS are supported natively; on Windows use Docker or WSL2.

$ git clone https://github.com/vmmc2/Bleach.git && cd Bleach/scripts && chmod +x *.sh
$ ./bleach_build.sh
$ ./bleach_run.sh

VERIFYING THE ARTIFACT

From scripts/, the same command works identically under Docker or a native build:

$ ./bleach_test_pipeline.sh
Bleach Test Suite Execution Summary
Total valid tests: 44
Passed valid tests: 44
Failed valid tests: 0
44 / 44regression tests passing — covers every AST node type
11 / 11algorithms & data structures run unmodified
0third-party dependencies (C++ standard library only)

A minimal smoke test — run the REPL and evaluate one expression:

$ ./bleach_run.sh
> print "Hello, World!";
Hello, World!

LICENSE

This project is licensed under the MIT License — see LICENSE in the archive for the full text.

LINKS

  • Source repository: github.com/vmmc2/Bleach
  • Language documentation: vmmc2.github.io/Bleach-Docs

metadata.title: ESTRATÉGIAS PEDAGÓGICAS PARA A SUPERAÇÃO DA DIFICULDADE ESCOLAR NO ENSINO DE QUÍMICA ORGÂNICA
metadata.description: O ensino de Química Orgânica enfrenta desafios significativos devido à sua complexidade inerente, que exige a articulação entre representações simbólicas e modelos submicroscópicos, resultando frequentemente em dificuldades de aprendizagem e memorização mecânica. Este trabalho apresenta o desenvolvimento e a aplicação do jogo de cartas intitulado: “Quem sou eu?”, uma estratégia pedagógica baseada em metodologias ativas voltada para facilitar a compreensão de funções orgânicas e nomenclaturas. A atividade foi realizada com 12 estudantes universitários vinculados aos programas PIBID, PIBIC e PET, utilizando cartas didáticas e dinâmicas de adivinhação por meio de pistas. A avaliação da metodologia, realizada via questionários, revelou 100% de aprovação dos participantes quanto à facilidade de compreensão do jogo, sua eficácia como ferramenta de revisão e sua adequação como complemento ao ensino tradicional. Os resultados indicam que a abordagem lúdica promove o engajamento discente, estimula o raciocínio lógico e favorece uma construção mais dinâmica e participativa do conhecimento químico.
